properties.title: Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks in Medical Imaging Classification: A Promising Solution for Deep Learning Limits in Data Scarcity Scenarios

properties.source_path: Papers/003_2023_Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks in Medical Imaging Classification A Promising Solution for Deep Learning Limits in Data Scarcity Scenarios.pdf
properties.version_basis: Published article PDF identified by SHA-256; title page read and confirmed.

properties.description: Retrospective single-center comparison of six image classifiers (deterministic CNN, dropout variants, dropout-Bayesian and fully Bayesian CNN) for three-class cardiac amyloidosis subtype classification from early [18F]-florbetaben PET slices.
Static single-image classifiers with and without weight-space uncertainty. No state, transition or action.
properties.world_model_status: not a world model; supporting-component candidate (provisional)

properties.population: retrospective subjects with AL-CA, ATTR-CA or CA-like suspicion at one institution
properties.decision: classify cardiac amyloidosis subtype from early PET slices
properties.autonomy: not stated; future clinical application is mentioned

properties.description: 1,107 heart-centered PET slices (375 AL, 312 ATTR, 420 CTRL) from 47 subjects at Fondazione Toscana Gabriele Monasterio, 2016 to 2020. Not available to others.
properties.label_provenance: clinical combination of investigations, with one passage stating cardiac biopsy; stated inconsistently

properties.description: 38 subjects (10 ATTR, 12 AL, 16 CTRL), 897 slices split 80/20 into 717 training and 180 validation; validation shares patients with training; training set augmented 5x to 4,302 images
9 held-out subjects (3 ATTR, 3 AL, 3 CTRL), 210 slices

Tables 2 to 6: accuracy on training, validation and test splits, validation-test mismatch, one-versus-all precision, recall and F1, and vote confidence, for six networks; mean (SD) statistic not stated

properties.algorithm: DropCNN, dropout p=0.25, inactive at evaluation
DropCNN, dropout p=0.5, inactive at evaluation
DropBCNN, dropout p=0.25, active at evaluation (approximate Bayesian)
DropBCNN, dropout p=0.5, active at evaluation (approximate Bayesian)
BCNN, Bayesian layers trained by Bayes-by-backprop

assertions.rationale: The model maps one static image to class probabilities. Figure 2 shows no recurrent, memory or carried-state element, and each subject contributes a single acquisition. The weight posterior is a distribution over parameters, not a carried state.
The BCNN keeps a posterior over weights, which is not a belief over a patient state, and no state exists to carry a belief.

relation_assertions.rationale: Static no-action classifier with an uncertainty estimator; V36 allows BP_COMPONENT with action and planner features not_applicable.

Reviewer mapping only. A weight-space uncertainty estimator for a static image classifier could inform a runtime-assurance module, but its confidence is not shown to be calibrated and the paper never discusses world models, so this is a tentative supporting-component rationale and not a capability of the paper.

capability_assessments.rationale: Verified from the methods and Figure 2: a feed-forward image classifier with one frame per subject, no carried state, no transition over time and no actions. Weight-space uncertainty and Monte Carlo sampling are not a state or a transition.

gate_assessments.rationale: The test split is patient level, but the unit of the training and validation split is not stated and the authors describe validation as sharing patients with training. Data are not available and the label provenance is stated two ways.
No state transition exists in a static classifier, so state-transition prediction evidence has no subject.
Vote confidence is reported but no calibration against observed frequencies, and no acceptance tolerance, is reported.
No external, subgroup or shifted-data validation. The held-out test is 9 patients from one institution.

legacy_cells.B: Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks in Medical Imaging Classification: A Promising Solution for Deep Learning Limits in Data Scarcity Scenarios
legacy_cells.C: Filippo Bargagna; Lisa Anita De Santi; Nicola Martini; Dario Genovesi; Brunella Favilli; Giuseppe Vergaro; Michele Emdin; Assuero Giorgetti; Vincenzo Positano; Maria Filomena Santarelli
legacy_cells.I: 003_2023_Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks in Medical Imaging Classification A Promising Solution for Deep Learning Limits in Data Scarcity Scenarios.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Cardiac amyloidosis (AL-CA and ATTR-CA; controls included)
legacy_cells.S: Can an uncertainty-aware classifier distinguish cardiac amyloidosis subtypes from early [18F]-florbetaben PET images?
legacy_cells.T: 47 subjects: 13 ATTR-CA patients, 15 AL-CA patients, and 19 control patients.
legacy_cells.V: Classify cardiac amyloidosis subtype from early PET images.
legacy_cells.AJ: Five convolutional modules followed by a three-linear-layer classifier; the BCNN uses Bayesian convolutional and linear layers.
legacy_cells.BI: Bayesian convolutional neural network (BCNN); comparison models: CNN, DropCNN, and DropBCNN.
legacy_cells.BT: Three-class softmax classification head for AL, ATTR, and control labels.
legacy_cells.BV: Cross-entropy loss; BCNN trained by variational inference (Bayes-by-backprop with local reparameterization).
legacy_cells.CS: Validation–test accuracy mismatch was used as an OOD-detection measure; BCNN mismatch was 6.14 (3.83)% (mean (SD)).
legacy_cells.EG: One-image classification latency: approximately 1.9 ms for CNN, DropCNN, and DropBCNN, and approximately 9.5 ms for BCNN; probabilistic inference used 100 samples.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with CNN, DropCNN (p=0.25, 0.5), and DropBCNN (p=0.25, 0.5); BCNN test accuracy 78.28 (1.99)% versus CNN 77.05 (2.88)% (mean (SD)).
legacy_cells.ER: AIFA committee and institutional ethics committee approval; the study states compliance with the Helsinki Declaration.
legacy_cells.FB: Direct PET-image-to-classification mapping; no persistent patient or scene state is defined.
legacy_cells.FL: Heart-centered PET slices are processed by five convolutional modules and a three-layer classifier; the BCNN substitutes Bayesian layers with Gaussian-mixture parameter priors and produces class probabilities/confidence estimates. No transition model or planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors develop and compare fully Bayesian and dropout-Bayesian convolutional classifiers for cardiac amyloidosis subtype classification under limited imaging data, with uncertainty estimates.
legacy_cells.FN: BCNN test accuracy was 78.28 (1.99)% and validation–test accuracy mismatch was 6.14 (3.83)%; the authors report improved mismatch/OOD detection versus comparator models and epistemic uncertainty estimates.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors identify the limited, disease-specific dataset and lack of a disease-severity index as limitations that may bias the data and split.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work: test the Bayesian framework in similar scenarios, develop a PET-based severity metric, and improve model tuning, Bayesian approximations, inference algorithms, and computational cost.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors motivate the work by reduced deep-learning performance and generalization with scarce medical data and by deterministic systems' inability to provide epistemic uncertainty.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to retrospective internal classification of early cardiac PET images. The study does not demonstrate a persistent state, temporal transitions, action-conditioned or causal effects, alternative-action rollouts, planning/control, prospective clinical utility, or external validation; OOD mismatch is a proxy metric, not evidence of clinical benefit.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M2 Encoders; M7 Outcome & causal layer; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Calibrate Bayesian imaging uncertainty and expose confidence to the safety gate; validate it separately from any later temporal model.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–2: title, byline, abstract and introduction; pp. 2–3: background/Bayesian neural networks; pp. 3–6: cardiac amyloidosis, cohort, data acquisition/preprocessing, architecture, implementation and hyperparameters; pp. 6–9: results and Tables 1–6, discussion, conclusion, and limitations; p. 9: data/code availability, ethics and disclosures; pp. 10–11: references and final page. Table 4's extracted row layout is interleaved; no extracted values rely on it. Tables 2 and 6 used for cited outcomes are legible. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I prefilled workbook fields were left untouched. The article studies retrospective PET-image classification; exclusion reflects static prediction with no demonstrated persistent state or temporal evolution. Table 4's text extraction is interleaved but was not used. The supplied files do not include the referenced KB module/open-problem definitions, so FS and FU were omitted rather than guessed. Evidence QA: 21/52 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (40.4%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Schema normalization (source details retained): DU normalized to 'Patient-level split'; source detail: Subjects were split into 38 for training/validation and 9 for testing; training/validation was split 80%/20%. The same datasets were used for all models. Codex audit: 51 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Legacy workbook columns were reviewed selectively; others remain imported-only (see coverage sidecar).
Supporting-component status is a reviewer judgment from the uncertainty-estimator reading; the paper itself never mentions world models. It stays provisional.
What the printed SDs and the p-values below 0.05 are taken over, and the test used, are not stated, so those uncertainties are recorded as printed.

Schema and quote occurrence do not prove entailment. Targeted second-model review confirms the separate nine-subject test cohort and the printed Table 6 anomaly; no independent human review or full second re-extraction.

22 November 2026: complete references1–32 plus declarations, licence and publisher note on pp10–11 read as bibliography/metadata. Figure1 p3 inspected directly: deterministic versus Bayesian layer/convolution schematic, not a dynamic-world experiment. Other figures/tables retain prior visual verification. Cited primary papers were not retrieved and their results are not inherited.
notes: Primary-method record. The legacy label (not a world model, supporting component, R2) was treated as a hypothesis and checked against the methods. The static single-image design is confirmed and the world-model classification stands as not_world_model. Source problems: validation shares patients with training, so the claimed OOD detection rests on a validation-test accuracy gap; the test set is 9 patients; Table 2 SDs are not defined; one Table 6 cell prints an implausible SD; label provenance is stated two ways. Revision r2: the legacy workbook already classifies this as supporting / not a world model; the earlier narrative calling it legacy core was mistaken. R2 is limited to the patient-separated internal test cohort; training–validation overlap and unvalidated OOD claims remain flagged.
